title: Antifragility Stress-Testing: Does Adding Models Reduce or Concentrate Tail Risk?

original_idea.body:
# Antifragility Stress-Testing

Estimate the tail of the fraction-of-panel-simultaneously-wrong distribution on hard safety judgments and test whether adding more homogeneous models thins or fattens the tail of catastrophic joint errors vs lineage-diverse scaling. Inference + tail statistics.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — examining the tail of joint catastrophic errors directly targets correlated catastrophic failure, the part that matters most.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: estimate tail of the simultaneously-wrong distribution; tail estimation with limited samples needs statistical care, guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (tail behavior vs panel scaling) but robust tail estimation is a real dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public models + risk-analysis toolkit, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: A fat-tail/antifragility tail-risk analysis of model-panel scaling appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No known tail-risk antifragility analysis of LLM panel scaling.
